notes: City of Asheville, NC (Buncombe County seat). Source is Buncombe County GIS's public opendata MapServer layer 1 ('Property') — geometry + 2026 tax-year land/building/total market values (still the 2021 reappraisal's: a 2026 state law postponed the new reappraisal to 2027) + property class + exemption code in one layer. See run_asheville.py.

City restriction uses the assessor's municipal TAX-DISTRICT code City='CAS' (not the mailing CityName), cross-checked symmetrically against a representative-point-within test on the county's Incorporated Areas polygon: IoU 99.98% (39,813 in both, 7 CAS outside, 1 non-CAS inside).

~33.6k shipped parcels ($18.4B taxable market value), served as PMTiles with H3 hexes below z12 (parquet_to_pmtiles.py --drop-remnants): the browser GeoParquet path froze Chrome for ~30 s building the 3D extrusions.
Improvements = total market value − land, i.e. the county's BuildingValue PLUS its 'Features' value (paving, outbuildings; $57.7M citywide).

NON-MAPPED PARCELS: Buncombe does not draw condo units (NmpType 0, PIN root+'C'+unit) or leasehold improvements (NmpType 3, root+'L'+id) — each carries an exact copy of its parent parcel's polygon, stacked up to 226 deep. run_asheville.py collapses each 10-digit PIN root onto the parent footprint, summing only the TAXABLE member accounts: 3,962 units + 53 leaseholds -> 242 parcels, 0 stacked footprints left.

CONDO LAND: Buncombe assigns condo units $0 land (the whole value is building) and the development's COMMON AREA parcel is $0 too, so downtown condos rendered as the cheapest land in the city. Like run_boston.py, the land of 222 condo lots is ESTIMATED from the land $/sqft of the 15 nearest built, non-condo parcels within 3x the lot's size (land $/sqft falls steeply with lot size), with a floor of the lower-quartile townhome/apartment land share (11%; the floor itself never exceeds the any-size neighbours' estimate), and capped at 70% of the lot's value. A lot with too few similar-sized parcels nearby (only Beaverdam Run, 99 acres) gets just the floor. Developments that also hold exempt units get land for their taxable share only: +$190M. The popup flags these as estimates. They carry condo_land_imputed = 1 with the county's figure in assessor_land_value, and are never labelled Underdeveloped.

NO VALUATION: parcels with $0 land AND $0 improvements are not shipped (they would render as the cheapest land): HOA common areas whose value the county folds into the surrounding homes, and lots / new construction the 2026 roll has not valued yet.

EXEMPT: EXM/RXM and the other institutional EX* codes, government-owned classes (when a government body owns the record or it carries no value) and exact-named government owners with no code yet (33 records, mostly 2025-26 NCDOT / UNC Health / County acquisitions) are excluded. Owner-level relief (ELD elderly, VET, DIS, HIS historic deferral, BLD builder inventory, BRF brownfield, EX2 pollution-abatement equipment) is on ordinary taxable property and KEPT. EX1/EX4 CCRCs (Givens Estates, Deerfield; $334M) could be partly taxable under G.S. 105-278.6A, but their 2026 tax bills show them fully exempt (Givens never billed; Deerfield taxable on $78,600), so they are excluded.

Excluded as non-land: state-assessed utility networks (800, 81x, 82x, 831, 836, 853) and right-of-way (305 road, 842 railroad). Cell-tower sites (830) and waste disposal / scrap yards (850/852) are ordinary taxable property and kept.
Land area is the geodesic polygon area: the source Acreage is on a 0.01-acre grid (up to ~10% rounding on small lots) and agrees with the polygon at median ratio 1.0001.

link is Buncombe's Spatialest property record card (per-parcel deep link supplied by the source layer's PropCard field). For a merged condo/leasehold lot it opens the PARENT lot, whose card shows only the lot's own value — record_note says so.

Review feed (review.html?city=asheville): data/scripts/build_review_feed.py --city asheville writes asheville-nc-review.json next to the parquet; upload it beside the parcel parquet and bump reviewVersion.

Parking: OSM-only extraction (parking_lot_extraction.py --osm-only, 2026-09-30): 436 lots, 294.8 acres, ~$206M estimated land value; the NAIP+ML satellite pass has not been run, so suburban/commercial lots missing from OSM are undercounted.
